title: One point blowup strictly decreases the weak-transform colength
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a regular local ring of Krull dimension $2$, let $I\subsetneq A$ be an ideal such that $A/I$ has finite length, and let $b:Y=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathfrak m}(\operatorname{Spec}A)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. Write $E=b^{-1}(\mathfrak m)$ for the exceptional effective Cartier divisor. There is a largest integer $d\geq0$ such that $I\mathcal O_Y\subseteq\mathcal O_Y(-dE)$, and $d\geq1$. Define $\mathcal J=I\mathcal O_Y(dE)\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$, where $\mathcal O_Y(-dE)$ is the $d$th power of the ideal of $E$ and $\mathcal O_Y(dE)$ is its inverse invertible module. The support of $\mathcal O_Y/\mathcal J$ is a finite set $S$ of closed points of $E$, and $$\sum_{q\in S}\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{Y,q}}(\mathcal O_{Y,q}/\mathcal J_q)<\operatorname{length}_A(A/I).$$ The empty set $S$ is allowed. Conventions: [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], [def-weil-pbc-module-length], [def-nagata-global-blowup], [def-nagata-extended-ideal], [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], [def-sc-invertible-module], [pqf-def-coherent].

source.place: Tag 0AGT, resolve-lemma-blowup-improve, statement and proof. Finite colength is equivalent to the displayed hypothesis that a power of the maximal ideal is contained in the proper ideal, by algebra.tex Tag 00L5 (algebra-lemma-support-point), proof, second paragraph.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-local-surface-maximal-blowup-geometry], $Y$ is Noetherian and regular and $E\cong\mathbf P^1_k$ is a nonempty integral effective Cartier divisor. Put $\mathcal L=\mathfrak m\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_Y(-E)$ and $\mathcal K=I\mathcal O_Y$. The equality defining $\mathcal L$ follows because the scheme-theoretic fibre is cut out by the extended maximal ideal. The ideal $\mathcal L$ is invertible by [lemma-nagata-effective-cartier-is-invertible].

source.place: Tags 0AGQ, 0AGR and 0AGT, exceptional divisor and its ideal.

proof.text: Choose a maximal strict submodule chain of $A/I$, of length $N=\operatorname{length}_A(A/I)\geq1$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Each factor is simple. A nonzero element identifies a simple module with $A/\mathfrak m$, since its annihilator is maximal and $A$ is local. Thus $\mathfrak m$ kills each factor and $\mathfrak m^N(A/I)=0$. Hence $\mathfrak m^N\subseteq I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, so $\mathcal L^N\subseteq\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal L$. On an affine $Y$-open with ring $R$, the fibre-product definition [def-nagata-extended-ideal] gives $R\otimes_A A/I=R/IR$; hence $\mathcal K$ is generated by the images of a finite generating set of $I$. It is quasi-coherent of finite type. Its quotients and the quotients by powers of $\mathcal L$ are likewise locally associated to finite modules; [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] makes them coherent. Outside $E$ the ideal $\mathcal L$ is the unit ideal, so $\mathcal K=\mathcal O_Y$ there.

source.place: Tag 0AGT, first paragraph; algebra.tex Tag 00L5 (lemma-support-point), finite-length direction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-single-cartier-divisorial-part] to $\mathcal K$ and $E$. It gives $a\geq0$, $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal L^a$, equality at the generic point $\eta$ of $E$, and residual support away from codimension one. Since $\mathcal K_\eta\subseteq\mathcal L_\eta$, necessarily $a\geq1$: a local equation $t$ for $E$ is a nonunit nonzerodivisor. The same cancellation shows $a\leq N$ from $\mathcal L^N\subseteq\mathcal K$. If $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal L^e$ with $e>a$, equality at $\eta$ gives $t^a\in t^{a+1}\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}$, whence $1\in(t)$, a contradiction. Thus $d=a$ is precisely the largest integer in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0AGT, first paragraph and invocation of divisors.tex Tag 0AGB.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal F=\mathcal L^d/\mathcal K$. The closed set $T$ supplied in step 3 is contained in $E$ and all its components have codimension at least two in $Y$. No such component is $E$: at the generic point of an integral effective Cartier divisor the divisor has codimension one, as in [lem-sfb-single-cartier-divisorial-part]. An integral projective line has only its generic point and closed points (on either affine chart, primes of $k[t]$ are $(0)$ or generated by an irreducible polynomial). Thus all points of $T$ are closed in $E$ and hence in $Y$. By [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-points-finite], $T$ is finite. The subset $S=\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F)\subseteq T$ is consequently finite and consists of closed exceptional points. Since $\mathcal F$ is coherent, [lem-sfb-coherent-zero-dimensional-support] gives $H^1(Y,\mathcal F)=0$, including $S=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0AGT, use of Tag 0AGB and the omitted finite-support higher-cohomology argument; coherent.tex Tag 0B3J.

proof.text: The finite generators of $I$ give a surjection from a finite sum of copies of $\mathcal O_Y$ onto $\mathcal K$, so [lem-sfb-maximal-point-blowup-generated-cohomology] gives $H^1(Y,\mathcal K)=0$. Apply the long exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] for module global sections [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology] to $0\to\mathcal K\to\mathcal O_Y\to\mathcal Q\to0$, where $\mathcal Q=\mathcal O_Y/\mathcal K$. It gives a surjection $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal Q)$. By [lem-sfb-regular-point-blowup-functions], the canonical map $A\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ is an isomorphism: the base is regular Noetherian of dimension two and the fibre $E$ is nonempty. Each element of $I$ maps to zero in $\mathcal Q$, hence the surjection factors through $A/I\twoheadrightarrow\Gamma(Y,\mathcal Q)$.

source.place: Tag 0AGT, first short exact sequence; 0AGS(3),(4), with existing blowup-functions node for clause (4).

proof.text: The inclusions $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal L^d\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ give $0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal Q\to\mathcal T\to0$ with $\mathcal T=\mathcal O_Y/\mathcal L^d$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] and $H^1(Y,\mathcal F)=0$, the sequence $0\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal Q)\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal T)\to0$ is exact. The image of the unit global section in $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal T)$ is nonzero: at any point of the nonempty $E$, its germ is $1\bmod t^d$, which is nonzero because $t$ is a nonunit and $d\geq1$. All these groups are $A$-modules via $b$.

source.place: Tag 0AGT, second short exact sequence and nonzero image of 1.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] first to the kernel sequence of $A/I\twoheadrightarrow\Gamma(Y,\mathcal Q)$ and then to the exact row of step 6. All lengths are finite and $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal T)\ne0$ has length at least one. Consequently $\operatorname{length}_A\Gamma(Y,\mathcal F)<\operatorname{length}_A\Gamma(Y,\mathcal Q)\leq\operatorname{length}_A(A/I)$.

source.place: Tag 0AGT, strict inequality from the exact diagram; algebra.tex Tag 00IV.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal J=\mathcal K\otimes\mathcal L^{-d}\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$. Locally choose a basis $v$ of $\mathcal L^d$, so $\mathcal K=vJ$ for an ideal $J$ and the quotient $\mathcal F$ becomes $R/J$. Tensoring with the inverse basis leaves this quotient unchanged. These maps glue to $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{-d}\cong\mathcal O_Y/\mathcal J$; they also show that $\mathcal J$ is exactly $I\mathcal O_Y(dE)$ and that the two quotients have the same nonzero-stalk support $S$. At each $q\in S$ a local basis gives an $\mathcal O_{Y,q}$-linear isomorphism $\mathcal F_q\cong\mathcal O_{Y,q}/\mathcal J_q$. This uses just the local rank-one definition [def-sc-invertible-module].

source.place: Tag 0AGT, final paragraph: invertible twist and local trivialization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-coherent-finite-support-skyscrapers] to the coherent sheaf $\mathcal F$ on the locally Noetherian $Y$ and its finite closed support $S$. Taking sections of its finite skyscraper sum gives the $A$-linear isomorphism $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal F)\cong\bigoplus_{q\in S}\mathcal F_q$, since each skyscraper has global sections its defining module. Repeated length additivity [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] therefore gives $\operatorname{length}_A\Gamma(Y,\mathcal F)=\sum_{q\in S}\operatorname{length}_A(\mathcal F_q)$. For each $q$, every strict chain of $\mathcal O_{Y,q}$-submodules is a strict chain of $A$-submodules via $A\to\mathcal O_{Y,q}$. The supremum definition [def-weil-pbc-module-length] gives $\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{Y,q}}(\mathcal F_q)\leq\operatorname{length}_A(\mathcal F_q)$. Combine this with the stalk isomorphisms of step 8 and step 7 to get the required strict inequality. For $S=\varnothing$ both the direct sum and its length are zero. No residue-field equality is assumed.
